passages.original: 17. Sed quoniam jam e cautibus et confragosis locis enavigavit oratio, pandenda sunt vela, et in epilogos illius irruendum, in quibus sciolus sibi vi- sus, Tertullianum in testimonium 2 vocat, et Vi- ctorini Petabionensis 3 episcopi verba proponit. Et de Tertulliano quidem nihil amplius dico, quam Ecclesiae hominem non fuisse. De Victorino vero id assero, quod et de evangelistis, fratres eum dixis- se Domini, non filios Mariae.
passages.english: 17. But since my discourse has now sailed clear of the rocks and rugged places, the sails must be spread and we must rush upon his concluding arguments, in which, thinking himself a man of some learning, he calls Tertullian as a witness and puts forward the words of Victorinus, bishop of Petavium. And of Tertullian indeed I say nothing more than that he was not a man of the Church. But concerning Victorinus I assert what [I asserted] also concerning the evangelists: that he called them brothers of the Lord, not sons of Mary.
passages.notes: 'Petabionensis' is the edition's spelling for Petavium (Poetovio, modern Ptuj); the digits 2 and 3 in the text are footnote marks and have been omitted. 'sciolus' implies a smatterer, one with superficial learning; 'thinking himself a man of some learning' renders the ironic sense.
